nodes.description: Car5a-null mice show hyperammonemia and impaired growth, with normal fasting glucose. Double knockout worsens hyperammonemia, growth and survival and reduces fasting glucose. Sodium-potassium citrate improved breeding and neonatal survival but did not improve growth or post-weaning mortality; efficacy in humans is unestablished.

nodes.description: Carglumic acid is an N-acetylglutamate analogue that activates CPS1. It has been used off-label for acute hyperammonemia in CA-VA deficiency, with rapid biochemical responses in uncontrolled clinical reports. Activation of residual CPS1 flux despite bicarbonate limitation is proposed; benefit cannot always be separated from concurrent caloric support and other ammonia-lowering measures.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic CA5A variants cause absent or reduced mitochondrial carbonic anhydrase VA activity. Patient liver and heterologous expression studies provide complementary evidence; residual activity is not a reliable predictor of clinical severity.
